newsitem.title: EGYPT: Ex-banker appointed to head Egyptian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Ex-banker appointed to head Egyptian bourse.

text.p: Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri appointed ex-banker Abdelghani Gamie as chairman of the Egyptian stock exchange on Monday under a new system which tightens state control of the institution.
He replaces Nassef Nazmi Girgis, a veteran broker who was elected by fellow brokers in 1995 along with all the other members of the exchange board.
Under the new system, established by presidential decree on Saturday, the brokerage companies will now elect only six members of an 11-member exchange board.

Gamie, who is 66, retired in 1990 after 37 years in banking, mostly with state-owned National Bank of Egypt (NBE). He served as deputy chairman of NBE and was later chairman of the state's Bank of Alexandria and chairman of Egyptian American Bank, in which Bank of Alexandria was then the majority shareholder.
He also helped establish two brokerage firms since 1993 and was their deputy chairman until his appointed to the bourse.
One member of the stock exchange board will represent the Central Bank of Egypt, one the Capital Market Authority (CMA) and two will represent banks.
The CMA has supervisory authority over the exchange.
